decision.summary: 31 of 34 findings are evidence-backed; 3 were insufficient and recorded for follow-up.

findings.statement: NVIDIA's AI computing offering consists of GPU‑based accelerated compute systems and related processors for AI and high‑performance computing workloads.
NVIDIA's data‑center platform is an integrated set of compute, system, networking, and software elements that customers can deploy as a service or in‑house.
NVIDIA targets cloud service providers and AI developers as primary customer groups for its AI computing and data‑center platforms.
NVIDIA currently sells its AI computing and data‑center offerings in the United States and Europe.
NVIDIA’s software ecosystem for AI developers includes CUDA and other AI software offerings that require framework, library, API, and container compatibility.
Availability of NVIDIA products on cloud providers must be confirmed for each provider, region, instance type, capacity, and date; partnership announcements alone are insufficient.

CSP evaluation of NVIDIA platforms includes accelerator supply, qualified system configurations, deployment lead time, serviceable capacity, and performance across training, fine‑tuning, and inference workloads.
Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) subscription is listed at $200–$400 per CPU core per year for typical mid‑market customers (Vendr pricing table).
Broadcom: VendorBenchmark reports VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) list pricing of $175–$240 per core per year in early 2026, before enterprise discounts.
Broadcom: VendorBenchmark lists VMware vSphere Foundation (VVF) at $70–$95 per core per year in early 2026.
Broadcom reported fiscal 2025 total revenue of $64 billion, a record 24 % year‑over‑year increase.

findings.statement: In fiscal 2025, Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue reached $20 billion, driving overall semiconductor revenue to $37 billion.
Broadcom's infrastructure software segment generated $27 billion in fiscal 2025, up 26 % year‑over‑year, largely from VMware Cloud Foundation sales.
Broadcom's Q4 fiscal 2025 infrastructure software revenue was $6.9 billion, a 19 % increase year‑over‑year, with total software bookings of $10.4 billion.
Broadcom released VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 (version 9.1) on October 15, 2026, as documented in the technical documentation portal.
Intel Corp: Intel's Data Center and AI segment reported $16.92 billion in revenue for fiscal 2025, up from $15.52 billion the previous year, a 9.01% year‑over‑year increase.
Mistral plans to use 13,800 Nvidia GPUs for a data center near Paris.
Deutsche Telekom’s Munich Industrial AI Cloud will be built with nearly 10,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs.
Nscale’s deployment will start with more than 12,600 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs and expand to over 66,000 GPUs by 2027.
The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU provides up to 20X higher performance over the prior generation.
The A100 80GB GPU offers memory bandwidth of over 2 terabytes per second (TB/s).
